Priyom —

Quick read: nothing catastrophic but a few items to push back on. High-level comments below and inline notes in the doc.

1) Data residency: We can commit to the US region for customer data that is identified as PII or regulated, but blanket US-only for all traffic for 12 months is operationally heavy. Proposal: US region by default for customer data + option for SparkBridge to request a specific region with 30-day notice and justification. Add requirement that region-specific routing is subject to capacity/availability.

2) Logs / Telemetry: 90 days is reasonable for inference logs (request/response metadata) but we need to define scope — not model weights, not full payload retention unless customer opts in. Suggest: default 90-day retention for request/response metadata; full payloads retained only per customer-configured retention policies with opt-in. Also mention automated deletion and audit logging for access.

3) DPA / KMS: We should offer customer-managed keys via KMS for Dedicated and Private deployments; for Hosted, we can offer KMS integration but will need an SLA caveat. We'll ask Security to confirm technical feasibility and SOW if they require on-prem.

4) Indemnity / Liability: Their indemnity language is broader than we accept. We should propose mutual indemnities, with a liability cap tied to fees paid in the prior 12 months and carveouts for third-party models/outputs and export-control events.

5) SOW acceptance criteria: tighten milestone acceptance windows to 5 business days and include objective test harness for latency/throughput acceptance. Avoid open-ended 'final acceptance' language.

I'll mark these in the redline and prepare a suggested counter. Laura — if you can verify the liability cap numbers and any required insurance minimums, that'd be great.

-Monica
Director, Commercial Contracts
Redwood Inference

Priyom / Monica —

I reviewed the indemnity and insurance asks. Proposed position: liability cap = aggregate monthly fees x 6 (or fees from prior 12 months, whichever is higher), with carveouts for gross negligence and willful misconduct. For insurance, we can accept the standard commercial general liability + cyber liability with $5M limit; refuse to take on product recall or third-party IP defense beyond mutual indemnity.

On the residency ask, we should confirm with Infra whether they can practically guarantee US-only routing for the pilot. If not, we accept the region-by-request model Monica suggested.

I'll draft the specific redline counters for indemnity and insert the insurance language to match standards.

Hi Julia / SparkBridge Contracts team —

Thanks for the redlines. We've gone through the packet internally and attached our counter-proposals (see attached: Redwood_Counter_SparkBridge_MSA_DPA_SOW_redlines.docx). High-level positions:

- Data residency: Redwood can commit to routing customer-designated regulated data to US regions by default for the duration of the pilot. For general traffic, we propose region routing by request with 30 days' notice; region commitments remain subject to capacity constraints documented in the SOW.
- Logs/Telemetry: We accept a 90-day retention window for request/response metadata (request IDs, timestamps, latency metrics) but request that full payload retention be configurable by the customer. We will implement automated deletion and provide audit logs for any access.
- KMS: For Dedicated or Private deployments, we can support customer-managed keys. For Hosted, we offer KMS integration with documented SLA implications.

- Liability & Indemnity: We propose mutual indemnities and an overall liability cap equal to the greater of (i) fees paid in the prior 12 months or (ii) 6 months' forecasted fees for the pilot period. Carveouts for third-party model outputs and export control incidents included.

- SOW acceptance: We tightened acceptance windows to 5 business days per milestone and added objective acceptance tests (latency & throughput harness).

Would you be open to a 30-minute call tomorrow (Wed) at 11:00 AM PT to walk through the redlines and lock down the pilot SOW? If so, we can prepare a mutually-agreed checklist to speed sign-off.

Thanks — look forward to getting this moving.

Best,
Priyom Das

Redwood Inference

2) Logs: We accept the 90-day metadata retention default; we'd like a short clause requiring Redwood to notify SparkBridge 30 days before any retention policy changes.

3) Liability: Procurement is okay to move to mutual indemnities and the proposed liability cap for the pilot, but they want a written example calculation in the SOW so both sides are aligned.

4) Next step: Let's take the call tomorrow at 11:00 AM PT. I'll send a calendar invite with the SparkBridge contracts and Tom (CTO) on. Please include whoever from Security/Infra can speak authoritatively about KMS and routing.
